` [Highlight start] Alcohol worsens sleep apnea by relaxing throat muscles, narrowing airways, and slowing the brain's response to low oxygen levels [Highlight end] ` . Even moderate or evening drinking can trigger more frequent and longer breathing pauses, louder snoring, and lower blood oxygen.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXQbxWeux7eFKkCM1U7_ERaQ85PLHYNalwYCPnj40rTHMiji4aNoIn6zoYBhqtYTrluBxWgydZMTvuaAH1_naMiB_XfR_c-SuPslyQwGeWyAfZ_0XxvHieWWwqNzTnjaxhAJlMf4wPDUbUfs8jCNOesiBSYXA3IT-NHA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESigEBxCJF181ibxqeomAozkMO8VgYpICS1FHCP0zP4xrpguZazbZ4S5kkNuqkCjZBXEgITYXumdY1SitV1mLzupX9sUzTLGgdUrpTNI_GFu7aj-FHdyl0ev97o5c7zKD7vSBSpG-hp7QEIn_TH7AJICQsdhKR-uWI3pDmCFIyo30WRHgJDNnr8XU2z5s)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXMwqQJ0HpsltXT8OHErSTabLOP1vbPfJFyAORNIyRhBwubFU4KXPw0tq2Xl67Fch4uqFvEvg9pGog5rygD6mPV17iuq8QkWVSDahLA33LKRK_MNFzoUxjRqjT02ZmQqdr20B5maVXmMo)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXDUPRr5_pZmKVMboqO8nSpKcDfbgRGTp3-2dl27YGiZM2kTOpk-R9TPMcE-btE35Gg2uvcpTZdTLGdlwA3L8y2wQAaUevoK3Vc7M_GaXzMe-kZEr50z4IisFfz1lB71gLczOKqc8)

### How Alcohol Affects Breathing and Sleep

- **Airway collapse:** As a muscle relaxant, alcohol loosens muscles in the throat and upper airway, making blockages more likely in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkwEBxCJF1zIDY6oul3NW4MevS50vC-g0VaxLq87vH2dOdnbz27z_pfnxMKVC4yHsZo3v5M1rjYg2EIbPDZUTLC5_7ra9nvzVcKBNhO1Ga5Sic4UpAi7oQftmwNNVQMMasRs733u0RW5v1Vwfx_ZDMwwH69D6J3QggTv1TsfcCcJygOiBEAyIemMdjlPS_8Qp29cNmJU)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESigEBxCJF181ibxqeomAozkMO8VgYpICS1FHCP0zP4xrpguZazbZ4S5kkNuqkCjZBXEgITYXumdY1SitV1mLzupX9sUzTLGgdUrpTNI_GFu7aj-FHdyl0ev97o5c7zKD7vSBSpG-hp7QEIn_TH7AJICQsdhKR-uWI3pDmCFIyo30WRHgJDNnr8XU2z5s)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXbZRDBqgWkDrQX2Z1FYQGThaIaVVaJiBA45DwxW7npQgihSMbE0-jreYnaz9JKiBOOTibhDKEP_cpxJBICxFqPaJaUH7Qo-7ufLDRd3twXqLiElGePJ8ya47Zf5b-AcXkrlWLTzSZr-UBi9EnNCBMoejeVBYlrw)
- **Duller arousal response:** Alcohol depresses the central nervous system, delaying the brain's wake-up signal when oxygen drops and prolonging apnea episodes.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESigEBxCJF181ibxqeomAozkMO8VgYpICS1FHCP0zP4xrpguZazbZ4S5kkNuqkCjZBXEgITYXumdY1SitV1mLzupX9sUzTLGgdUrpTNI_GFu7aj-FHdyl0ev97o5c7zKD7vSBSpG-hp7QEIn_TH7AJICQsdhKR-uWI3pDmCFIyo30WRHgJDNnr8XU2z5s)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXQbxWeux7eFKkCM1U7_ERaQ85PLHYNalwYCPnj40rTHMiji4aNoIn6zoYBhqtYTrluBxWgydZMTvuaAH1_naMiB_XfR_c-SuPslyQwGeWyAfZ_0XxvHieWWwqNzTnjaxhAJlMf4wPDUbUfs8jCNOesiBSYXA3IT-NHA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXcWw3eP1KAw4CN19Klw28xA15SJ7TK5ydeoTny108kc_WsiymbGeykVKULLpqO6NLYy1WCrb1V0TocFor3lP2BmXRSr0_4-aEGh5fdiUkrDGWMm4qTtKq2QAF1pUCk31Ul-CH-LOLbw)
- **Central sleep apnea (CSA) impact:** Depressing the central nervous system can also disrupt signaling between the brain and breathing muscles, worsening CSA.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXbZRDBqgWkDrQX2Z1FYQGThaIaVVaJiBA45DwxW7npQgihSMbE0-jreYnaz9JKiBOOTibhDKEP_cpxJBICxFqPaJaUH7Qo-7ufLDRd3twXqLiElGePJ8ya47Zf5b-AcXkrlWLTzSZr-UBi9EnNCBMoejeVBYlrw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXQbxWeux7eFKkCM1U7_ERaQ85PLHYNalwYCPnj40rTHMiji4aNoIn6zoYBhqtYTrluBxWgydZMTvuaAH1_naMiB_XfR_c-SuPslyQwGeWyAfZ_0XxvHieWWwqNzTnjaxhAJlMf4wPDUbUfs8jCNOesiBSYXA3IT-NHA)
- **Fragmented sleep:** While alcohol may make you sleepy initially, metabolizing it later in the night disrupts REM sleep and causes nighttime awakenings.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXMwqQJ0HpsltXT8OHErSTabLOP1vbPfJFyAORNIyRhBwubFU4KXPw0tq2Xl67Fch4uqFvEvg9pGog5rygD6mPV17iuq8QkWVSDahLA33LKRK_MNFzoUxjRqjT02ZmQqdr20B5maVXmMo)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkwEBxCJF1zIDY6oul3NW4MevS50vC-g0VaxLq87vH2dOdnbz27z_pfnxMKVC4yHsZo3v5M1rjYg2EIbPDZUTLC5_7ra9nvzVcKBNhO1Ga5Sic4UpAi7oQftmwNNVQMMasRs733u0RW5v1Vwfx_ZDMwwH69D6J3QggTv1TsfcCcJygOiBEAyIemMdjlPS_8Qp29cNmJU)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXDUPRr5_pZmKVMboqO8nSpKcDfbgRGTp3-2dl27YGiZM2kTOpk-R9TPMcE-btE35Gg2uvcpTZdTLGdlwA3L8y2wQAaUevoK3Vc7M_GaXzMe-kZEr50z4IisFfz1lB71gLczOKqc8)
- **Long-term risk:** Higher alcohol intake is linked to an increased risk of sleep apnea and can contribute to weight gain, which further strains breathing during sleep.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXmqVmKdpZh__BBZJXQ7jQ7Tr3iv93FCyT0sCM1IehvH5uHzmWJmwEnHoutekBI78zu7cGNF6ALgPRLFqriujmAlare27VzwB3LmDK4s03MoJ2k0AyDBLuDrz5nIlzxpSJlQsdPCDaUQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXbG21KRn9pBWIwQUtQpfu1ZlNCD0wEjap-7-IL-5TGhlD0WoP3z-0lqgdpq0qpaa1Skolu8NCnaNUcuVi13K2Beyy3uvCo2tkz6AhoCnXwRp2AypLgwy1GHMa4iR22XXy8lBCO3CCuyUUqPdMIdg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXbZRDBqgWkDrQX2Z1FYQGThaIaVVaJiBA45DwxW7npQgihSMbE0-jreYnaz9JKiBOOTibhDKEP_cpxJBICxFqPaJaUH7Qo-7ufLDRd3twXqLiElGePJ8ya47Zf5b-AcXkrlWLTzSZr-UBi9EnNCBMoejeVBYlrw)

### Practical Steps to Reduce Risks

- **Avoid or cut back before bed:** Skipping evening alcohol is the most reliable way to prevent alcohol-related worsening. If you drink, stop at least **3 to 4 hours before bedtime** and keep intake low.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXQbxWeux7eFKkCM1U7_ERaQ85PLHYNalwYCPnj40rTHMiji4aNoIn6zoYBhqtYTrluBxWgydZMTvuaAH1_naMiB_XfR_c-SuPslyQwGeWyAfZ_0XxvHieWWwqNzTnjaxhAJlMf4wPDUbUfs8jCNOesiBSYXA3IT-NHA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXbZRDBqgWkDrQX2Z1FYQGThaIaVVaJiBA45DwxW7npQgihSMbE0-jreYnaz9JKiBOOTibhDKEP_cpxJBICxFqPaJaUH7Qo-7ufLDRd3twXqLiElGePJ8ya47Zf5b-AcXkrlWLTzSZr-UBi9EnNCBMoejeVBYlrw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkwEBxCJF1zIDY6oul3NW4MevS50vC-g0VaxLq87vH2dOdnbz27z_pfnxMKVC4yHsZo3v5M1rjYg2EIbPDZUTLC5_7ra9nvzVcKBNhO1Ga5Sic4UpAi7oQftmwNNVQMMasRs733u0RW5v1Vwfx_ZDMwwH69D6J3QggTv1TsfcCcJygOiBEAyIemMdjlPS_8Qp29cNmJU)
- **Keep using CPAP:** Wear your CPAP machine consistently even if you have had a drink, as it helps keep the airway open and counteracts breathing disruptions. Note that alcohol can cause nasal congestion, dry mouth, or mask leaks that make therapy less comfortable.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXQbxWeux7eFKkCM1U7_ERaQ85PLHYNalwYCPnj40rTHMiji4aNoIn6zoYBhqtYTrluBxWgydZMTvuaAH1_naMiB_XfR_c-SuPslyQwGeWyAfZ_0XxvHieWWwqNzTnjaxhAJlMf4wPDUbUfs8jCNOesiBSYXA3IT-NHA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXMwqQJ0HpsltXT8OHErSTabLOP1vbPfJFyAORNIyRhBwubFU4KXPw0tq2Xl67Fch4uqFvEvg9pGog5rygD6mPV17iuq8QkWVSDahLA33LKRK_MNFzoUxjRqjT02ZmQqdr20B5maVXmMo)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXbZRDBqgWkDrQX2Z1FYQGThaIaVVaJiBA45DwxW7npQgihSMbE0-jreYnaz9JKiBOOTibhDKEP_cpxJBICxFqPaJaUH7Qo-7ufLDRd3twXqLiElGePJ8ya47Zf5b-AcXkrlWLTzSZr-UBi9EnNCBMoejeVBYlrw)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESigEBxCJF181ibxqeomAozkMO8VgYpICS1FHCP0zP4xrpguZazbZ4S5kkNuqkCjZBXEgITYXumdY1SitV1mLzupX9sUzTLGgdUrpTNI_GFu7aj-FHdyl0ev97o5c7zKD7vSBSpG-hp7QEIn_TH7AJICQsdhKR-uWI3pDmCFIyo30WRHgJDNnr8XU2z5s)
- **Watch out for sedatives:** Avoid combining alcohol with sleeping pills, opioids, or other sedatives, which can dangerously suppress breathing.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXX0g8YJszrjDR6nhiZgcJ1z0fUrgjHu7Em9LPLmCUEKlC4vxtgYvC3IwPzYL-3ND1cyIi8d3eSwF8K1Ulq6KtbrT_p2S8cK7mABlQ9pxOPlAVgfmTpD-RJlL7m2lM7zPBW)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkwEBxCJF1zIDY6oul3NW4MevS50vC-g0VaxLq87vH2dOdnbz27z_pfnxMKVC4yHsZo3v5M1rjYg2EIbPDZUTLC5_7ra9nvzVcKBNhO1Ga5Sic4UpAi7oQftmwNNVQMMasRs733u0RW5v1Vwfx_ZDMwwH69D6J3QggTv1TsfcCcJygOiBEAyIemMdjlPS_8Qp29cNmJU)

For more details on symptoms, treatment effects, and management strategies, see [SleepApnea.org](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXbZRDBqgWkDrQX2Z1FYQGThaIaVVaJiBA45DwxW7npQgihSMbE0-jreYnaz9JKiBOOTibhDKEP_cpxJBICxFqPaJaUH7Qo-7ufLDRd3twXqLiElGePJ8ya47Zf5b-AcXkrlWLTzSZr-UBi9EnNCBMoejeVBYlrw), [Sleep Foundation](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXQbxWeux7eFKkCM1U7_ERaQ85PLHYNalwYCPnj40rTHMiji4aNoIn6zoYBhqtYTrluBxWgydZMTvuaAH1_naMiB_XfR_c-SuPslyQwGeWyAfZ_0XxvHieWWwqNzTnjaxhAJlMf4wPDUbUfs8jCNOesiBSYXA3IT-NHA) , or this [systematic review and meta-analysis](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXmqVmKdpZh__BBZJXQ7jQ7Tr3iv93FCyT0sCM1IehvH5uHzmWJmwEnHoutekBI78zu7cGNF6ALgPRLFqriujmAlare27VzwB3LmDK4s03MoJ2k0AyDBLuDrz5nIlzxpSJlQsdPCDaUQ).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXbZRDBqgWkDrQX2Z1FYQGThaIaVVaJiBA45DwxW7npQgihSMbE0-jreYnaz9JKiBOOTibhDKEP_cpxJBICxFqPaJaUH7Qo-7ufLDRd3twXqLiElGePJ8ya47Zf5b-AcXkrlWLTzSZr-UBi9EnNCBMoejeVBYlrw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXQbxWeux7eFKkCM1U7_ERaQ85PLHYNalwYCPnj40rTHMiji4aNoIn6zoYBhqtYTrluBxWgydZMTvuaAH1_naMiB_XfR_c-SuPslyQwGeWyAfZ_0XxvHieWWwqNzTnjaxhAJlMf4wPDUbUfs8jCNOesiBSYXA3IT-NHA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXmqVmKdpZh__BBZJXQ7jQ7Tr3iv93FCyT0sCM1IehvH5uHzmWJmwEnHoutekBI78zu7cGNF6ALgPRLFqriujmAlare27VzwB3LmDK4s03MoJ2k0AyDBLuDrz5nIlzxpSJlQsdPCDaUQ)Are you looking into this for yourself or someone else? items.text: Airway collapse: As a muscle relaxant, alcohol loosens muscles in the throat and upper airway, making blockages more likely in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Duller arousal response: Alcohol depresses the central nervous system, delaying the brain's wake-up signal when oxygen drops and prolonging apnea episodes. Central sleep apnea (CSA) impact: Depressing the central nervous system can also disrupt signaling between the brain and breathing muscles, worsening CSA. Fragmented sleep: While alcohol may make you sleepy initially, metabolizing it later in the night disrupts REM sleep and causes nighttime awakenings. Long-term risk: Higher alcohol intake is linked to an increased risk of sleep apnea and can contribute to weight gain, which further strains breathing during sleep.

- **Long-term risk:** Higher alcohol intake is linked to an increased risk of sleep apnea and can contribute to weight gain, which further strains breathing during sleep.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXmqVmKdpZh__BBZJXQ7jQ7Tr3iv93FCyT0sCM1IehvH5uHzmWJmwEnHoutekBI78zu7cGNF6ALgPRLFqriujmAlare27VzwB3LmDK4s03MoJ2k0AyDBLuDrz5nIlzxpSJlQsdPCDaUQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXbG21KRn9pBWIwQUtQpfu1ZlNCD0wEjap-7-IL-5TGhlD0WoP3z-0lqgdpq0qpaa1Skolu8NCnaNUcuVi13K2Beyy3uvCo2tkz6AhoCnXwRp2AypLgwy1GHMa4iR22XXy8lBCO3CCuyUUqPdMIdg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXbZRDBqgWkDrQX2Z1FYQGThaIaVVaJiBA45DwxW7npQgihSMbE0-jreYnaz9JKiBOOTibhDKEP_cpxJBICxFqPaJaUH7Qo-7ufLDRd3twXqLiElGePJ8ya47Zf5b-AcXkrlWLTzSZr-UBi9EnNCBMoejeVBYlrw)

items.title: Practical Steps to Reduce Risks
items.text: Avoid or cut back before bed: Skipping evening alcohol is the most reliable way to prevent alcohol-related worsening. If you drink, stop at least 3 to 4 hours before bedtime and keep intake low. Keep using CPAP: Wear your CPAP machine consistently even if you have had a drink, as it helps keep the airway open and counteracts breathing disruptions. Note that alcohol can cause nasal congestion, dry mouth, or mask leaks that make therapy less comfortable. Watch out for sedatives: Avoid combining alcohol with sleeping pills, opioids, or other sedatives, which can dangerously suppress breathing.
